video_directives: Within-scene stillness: character holds a single pose 2-4s inside scenes (0-2s, 13-17s, 21-23s) — add idle breathing/blink micro-motion so held diagram beats don't read frozen
Scene changes land well with eased transitions and varied compositions; keep this rhythm — it's the edit's strongest asset
Cross-fade overlaps (3s, 6-7s, 11-12s, 20s) show exposed intermediate frames — tighten transition duration or switch to clean cut-in/cut-out to avoid muddy blend frames

top3_directives: The 'THE OCEAN?' sub-line floats awkwardly mid-sky with no visual anchor — either merge it into the main headline lockup or give it a pill/badge treatment so it reads as intentional
Sun rays cut directly through the headline text zone, slightly muddying letter edges — dim or reposition rays so text sits on clean background
Large dead zone in the mid-left ocean band (empty horizon strip) — add a subtle layer element (island, bird, wave accent) or push the horizon line down to tighten composition
Fill the large empty blue band between the sun rays and 'NOPE.' with a subtle secondary element (bird, drifting cloud) to tighten the vertical eye path
Add a faint drop shadow or darker outline behind 'NOPE.' so it pops identically over both sky and sea bands
Give the character a slightly stronger rim glow or scale bump (5-8%) to fully separate it from the horizon line crossing behind its head
Large empty sand band in the bottom third — either push the character lower/larger or add subtle dune texture to reduce the dead zone
The mid-frame horizontal stripe artifacts across the sky and dunes look like rendering seams — clean or remove them
Title card's dark navy plate edges are hard against the sky; add a soft shadow or slight transparency for integration
Remove the semi-transparent horizontal stripe artifacts at the horizon line behind the character — they read as rendering errors
Fix the cloud cropped mid-shape at the right edge; either pull it fully in-frame or push it fully out
Fill the upper-left sky dead zone with a subtle secondary element (bird, faint gradient, distant dune line) to guide the eye from text to character
Fill the dead zones in the upper-right and bottom-third with subtle atmosphere (stars/dust, ground shadow detail) so the vertical canvas isn't empty

Clarify the scatter diagram's story: the incoming ray, fan of scattered rays, and outgoing ray overlap ambiguously — thicken/differentiate the primary ray so the eye path sun→scatter→eye is legible in one second
Anchor the character to a scene edge or frame line rather than floating in open sky; currently the figure reads as pasted below the panel
Fill the lower ~55% of the dark panel — it's a large dead zone; enlarge/recenter the scattering cloud cluster and rays to occupy the full card.
Thicken and brighten the light rays (especially the thin blue streaks and the stray orange ray) so the diagram reads at a glance on a 6-inch daylight screen.
Anchor the label pill fully inside or fully outside the panel edge — right now it straddles the card border, creating a muddy overlap where the glow text meets the frame corner.
The blue grid tiles sit close to the blue background value — push background darker or tiles lighter so the grid reads instantly on a daylight phone screen
The single amber lamp is the story beat but blends into the pattern; give it a stronger glow or scale bump so the eye finds it in under a second
The moon/sun at top and the header pill compete in the upper third — nudge the pill down slightly or dim the moon so the header owns that zone
Fill or shrink the large blue card — it's ~70% empty, creating a big dead zone with only 'DEEP' floating in it
Clarify the relationship between 'DEEP' and 'TOWARD SUN' — right now they read as two unrelated labels; unify as one diagram with a connecting visual cue
Ground the character with stronger connection to the card (e.g., have the pointing hand overlap the card edge) so the eye path character → sun → card is explicit
Fill the mid-left and lower-right dead zones with subtle secondary elements (birds, small clouds, parallax hills) to tighten the composition
Give the beam's ground ellipse a warm tint so the UFO-to-character eye path reads more clearly — the beam currently points at nothing
Add a subtle drop shadow or outline to the 'NOT A MIRROR' label's red underline so it separates cleanly from the blue background at small sizes
Fill or crop the large empty sky zones (left/right of character and below the pill) — the bottom third is a dead zone
The dots inside the whiteboard panel are faint and low-contrast; boost saturation/size so the red-vs-blue concept reads at a glance
Anchor the character visually to the panel (shadow, gaze, or pointer) so the eye path is sun → panel → character → caption instead of two disconnected subjects
Anchor the character properly: the feet/shadow ellipse relationship looks detached — feet should contact the shadow plane, and the single green shoe reads as an asset error
Fill the dead zone between the headline and the horizon line (roughly y 900–1100) with a secondary visual beat or push the character larger into that space
Rebalance the empty left half: the character is hard-parked bottom-right while clouds/blur squares float top-left — either crop composition tighter or add a mid-left depth element at character scale
